ideas.name: VoltVault
ideas.problem: The lack of standardized component specifications and compatibility data for micro-mobility hardware forces users to replace entire units when a single component like a controller or battery fails.
ideas.targetUser: DIY micro-mobility enthusiasts, urban commuters who perform their own repairs, and independent e-bike/scooter repair technicians seeking verified part interoperability.
coreFeatures: Component Digital Twin: A detailed digital profile for every registered part (e.g., controller voltage, phase wires, BMS protocols, and physical dimensions).
Compatibility Matchmaker: A search engine that cross-references part specs to suggest compatible replacement components from different manufacturers.
Battery Lifecycle Ledger: A diagnostic log to track charge cycles, voltage sag, and estimated remaining capacity to predict failure before it happens.
Crowdsourced Teardown Wiki: A community-driven database where users upload technical specs and photos from disassembled hardware to assist others.
realDependencies: Manufacturer API integrations for real-time component specifications
BMS (Battery Management System) Bluetooth/IoT connectivity for live telemetry
E-commerce marketplace APIs (eBay, AliExpress) for live part availability
Cloud database (Firebase or PostgreSQL) for massive component registry storage
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local JSON manifest acting as the 'Global Component Registry' containing pre-defined specs for common models like Xiaomi, Segway, and generic e-bike kits. For live telemetry, a 'Simulated BMS Engine' will use a random-walk algorithm to generate realistic voltage fluctuations and temperature drifts over time. All API calls will be routed through a mock service layer that implements artificial latency (800ms-1500ms) and randomized 'success/failure' responses to simulate real-world network instability.

ideas.name: Loom & Lore
ideas.niche: Circular luxury fashion provenance and maintenance tracking
ideas.problem: High-end resale markets lack verifiable proof of garment care and material integrity, leading to valuation uncertainty and loss of trust between buyers and sellers.
ideas.targetUser: Affluent capsule wardrobe owners and luxury vintage collectors (ages 25-50) who prioritize sustainability and want to maximize the ROI of their high-value apparel investments.
coreFeatures: Digital Wardrobe Vault: A high-fidelity catalog for storing material composition, brand origin, and purchase documentation.
Immutable Care Chronology: A time-stamped ledger for logging professional dry cleaning, tailor repairs, and seasonal storage conditions.
Provenance Report Generator: One-click creation of a 'Digital Certificate of Care' to share with luxury resale platforms or prospective buyers.
Smart Care Alerts: Automated notifications based on fabric type (e.g., 'Time to inspect your cashmere for pilling' or 'Professional cleaning recommended after 3 wears').
realDependencies: Computer Vision API (e.g., Google Cloud Vision) for textile and brand recognition
Blockchain Network (e.g., Polygon) for creating immutable ownership and care records
OCR Engine (e.g., AWS Textract) to extract data from physical care labels
Cloud Object Storage (e.g., AWS S3) for high-resolution garment photography
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a 'Mock Service Layer' that intercepts all API calls. For Vision/OCR, it will map specific dummy filenames to pre-defined JSON metadata (e.g., 'label_01.jpg' returns '100% Silk, Dry Clean Only'). Blockchain transactions will use a 'Simulated Consensus' delay of 2500ms followed by a hardcoded transaction hash. All 'uploads' will be handled by a local directory of high-res stock fashion images to mimic S3 behavior, and care alerts will be triggered by a simulated system clock rather than real-world usage patterns.

ideas.name: BloomLoop
ideas.niche: Hyper-local circular economy for micro-scale organic feedstock exchange.
ideas.problem: Small food businesses produce high-value organic waste (like coffee grounds or spent grain) that is too small for industrial waste services, while urban farmers struggle to find consistent, high-quality, nearby substrate sources.
ideas.targetUser: Urban café owners, craft brewers, and micro-bakeries looking to reduce waste costs; and small-scale mushroom cultivators, vermicomposters, and urban farmers seeking specific organic inputs.
coreFeatures: Feedstock Marketplace: A real-time directory of available organic streams categorized by type, weight, and frequency.
Smart Match Engine: Automated geolocation-based alerts when a producer's required substrate becomes available within a specific radius.
Micro-Logistics Scheduler: A lightweight coordination tool for scheduling hand-offs or small-batch pickups via e-cargo bike or walking.
Sustainability Impact Tracker: A dashboard generating 'Waste Diverted' and 'Carbon Offset' metrics for business marketing and ESG reporting.
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform (Geocoding and Distance Matrix API)
Stripe API (for micro-transaction fees or subscription management)
Firebase (for real-time database and user authentication)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a static JSON manifest of 20 pre-defined users and 10 'active' feedstock listings centered around a mock neighborhood (e.g., Brooklyn, NY). Map functionality will be simulated using a static image or a simple SVG overlay where clicking pins triggers data from the local manifest. All API calls will be wrapped in an 'AsyncEmulator' class that uses setTimeout to introduce artificial latency (800ms to 2500ms) and returns 'Success' or 'Network Error' objects randomly. Notifications will be simulated via a local setInterval that triggers a UI toast message every 45 seconds to mimic a new match being found.

ideas.niche: Residential electrification subsidy and ROI optimization
ideas.problem: The fragmentation and complexity of federal, state, and local energy-efficiency rebates create 'decision paralysis,' preventing homeowners from accessing significant savings on green retrofits.
ideas.targetUser: Homeowners aged 30-55, middle-to-high income, residing in areas with high energy costs and active green energy legislation (e.g., CA, NY, WA) who are planning major home upgrades.
coreFeatures: Interactive ROI Simulator
Geo-Targeted Incentive Matcher
Step-by-Step Subsidy Roadmap
Real-Time Rebate Availability Tracker
realDependencies: Attom Data API for property specs
ideas.emulationStrategy: Implement a Mock API layer that intercepts all network requests. Use a locally stored JSON file containing diverse regional profiles (zip codes, utility rates, incentive levels) to simulate geolocation-based results. Apply a 'Simulated Latency' wrapper to all calls, adding a random delay between 1.5 and 3 seconds. The 'Live Tracker' will use a seeded random function to simulate budget depletion, making the UI feel dynamic and urgent without a real backend.

ideas.name: WarpWise
ideas.niche: Technical textile repair and visible mending planning
ideas.problem: The 'knowledge gap' between seeing an aesthetic mending photo and knowing which specific thread weight, needle size, and stitch pattern are technically compatible with a specific garment's fabric weight and damage type.
ideas.targetUser: Eco-conscious Gen Z and Millennial hobbyists engaged in 'slow fashion' who possess basic sewing tools but lack formal textile engineering or advanced tailoring expertise.
coreFeatures: Damage Diagnostic Engine (Photo-to-Technical-Specs)
Pattern-to-Fabric Compatibility Matrix
Material Specification Calculator (Thread Weight & Needle Size)
Mend Recipe Project Planner & Stash Tracker
realDependencies: Computer Vision API (e.g., TensorFlow or Google Cloud Vision) for damage and fabric texture recognition
E-commerce Search API (e.g., Etsy or Amazon Associates) for real-time material sourcing
Cloud Database (e.g., Firebase or Supabase) for user project and material inventory storage
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'MockService' layer to intercept all network requests. The Computer Vision engine will be emulated by accepting any image upload, displaying a 2.5-second 'Analyzing Texture...' loading animation, and then returning a randomized but realistic result from a 'DamageManifest.json' file. The E-commerce API will be faked by returning a static array of curated sewing products mapped to the selected repair type. All data persistence (stashes/plans) will be handled via LocalStorage, and all 'server' responses will use a utility function to inject a random 500ms-1500ms delay to simulate real-world latency.
